pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #11 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is NOT matter? (1 mark)
   A. Light from a torch
   B. Air
   C. Milk
   D. A stone

2. Steam from a boiling pot is really (1 mark)
   A. A red liquid
   B. A block of ice
   C. A white solid
   D. An invisible gas

3. What happens to a liquid when you pour it into a different container? (1 mark)
   A. It disappears
   B. It keeps its old shape
   C. It becomes a solid
   D. It takes the shape of the new container

4. An empty bottle is full of (1 mark)
   A. Nothing
   B. Air
   C. Water
   D. Sand

5. How many millilitres are in 2 litres? (1 mark)
   A. 20
   B. 2000
   C. 200
   D. 20 000

6. Which grouping of gases is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Stone, water and wood are liquids
   B. Air, steam and cooking gas are gases
   C. Milk, chalk and steam are solids
   D. Sugar, oil and air are solids

7. Which of these is a liquid? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking oil
   B. Air in a football
   C. Chalk
   D. Sugar

8. Which of these is a danger of solid waste? (1 mark)
   A. It cleans rivers
   B. It blocks drains and causes floods
   C. It grows food
   D. It makes air fresh

9. Which of these is a benefit of proper waste management? (1 mark)
   A. More disease
   B. More floods
   C. A clean and healthy environment
   D. More flies

10. Which is an example of recycling? (1 mark)
   A. Melting scrap metal to make new items
   B. Using a tin for a pencil holder
   C. Buying less food
   D. Throwing paper in a bin

11. What should you do after handling waste? (1 mark)
   A. Wash hands with soap and clean water
   B. Wipe hands on your clothes
   C. Touch your face
   D. Eat at once

12. What does reuse mean? (1 mark)
   A. Bury it
   B. Use something again
   C. Throw it away
   D. Burn it

13. Why is broken glass on the ground dangerous? (1 mark)
   A. It rots
   B. It can cut people and animals
   C. It grows
   D. It feeds the soil

14. A wrapper of biscuits is made of plastic. Which type of waste is it? (1 mark)
   A. Decomposable
   B. Non-decomposable
   C. Liquid
   D. Gas

15. What does reduce mean? (1 mark)
   A. Make into new items
   B. Make less waste
   C. Burn waste
   D. Use again

16. Which of these is a way of protecting water sources? (1 mark)
   A. Washing clothes in the river
   B. Planting trees near rivers
   C. Throwing waste in the river
   D. Letting animals dirty the spring

17. What does water conservation mean? (1 mark)
   A. Using water carefully and protecting water sources
   B. Wasting water
   C. Boiling water
   D. Selling water

18. Which of these reduces water use when brushing teeth? (1 mark)
   A. Using a bucket of water
   B. Using a cup of water
   C. Using a hose
   D. Leaving the tap running

19. Which of these is a way to save water when bathing? (1 mark)
   A. Use a basin
   B. Leave the tap open
   C. Use a hose
   D. Use a sprinkler

20. Why should you keep drinking water in a clean covered container? (1 mark)
   A. To make it hot
   B. To make it salty
   C. To keep it safe from germs
   D. To make it colder

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Give three safety measures during waste management. (3 marks)

22. Explain why steam from a kettle is invisible although we see a white cloud above the spout. Say what state of matter the cloud is. (5 marks)

23. Explain why plastic bags are a danger to the environment. (3 marks)

24. Describe how you would organise the cleaning of a school compound using safe methods. (5 marks)

25. Explain why a rainwater tank should have a lid. (3 marks)

26. Describe the methods of conserving water. Include reducing, reusing and recycling with examples. (5 marks)

27. Describe how you would show that air takes up space using a cup, tissue paper and a basin of water. (4 marks)

28. Give two reasons why solids are useful in daily life. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #11 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Light from a torch
   Light has no mass and takes up no space.

2. D — An invisible gas
   Steam is water as a gas and is invisible. The cloud we see is tiny water drops.

3. D — It takes the shape of the new container
   A liquid has no shape of its own.

4. B — Air
   An empty bottle contains air.

5. B — 2000
   2 x 1000 = 2000 ml.

6. B — Air, steam and cooking gas are gases
   Air, steam and cooking gas are gases.

7. A — Cooking oil
   Cooking oil flows and takes the shape of its container.

8. B — It blocks drains and causes floods
   Waste blocks drains and water floods the area.

9. C — A clean and healthy environment
   Proper waste management protects health and the environment.

10. A — Melting scrap metal to make new items
   Melting metal to make new items is recycling.

11. A — Wash hands with soap and clean water
   Washing removes germs.

12. B — Use something again
   To reuse is to use again.

13. B — It can cut people and animals
   Sharp glass can injure.

14. B — Non-decomposable
   Plastic wrappers do not rot easily.

15. B — Make less waste
   To reduce is to make less waste.

16. B — Planting trees near rivers
   Tree roots hold the soil and protect water.

17. A — Using water carefully and protecting water sources
   Conservation means saving water and using it wisely.

18. B — Using a cup of water
   A cup uses only a little water.

19. A — Use a basin
   Using a basin limits the water used.

20. C — To keep it safe from germs
   Covered clean containers protect water.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wear gloves and closed shoes, use a rake or shovel, do not touch sharp objects, wash hands afterwards, do not burn waste.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

22. (5 marks)
   Answer: Steam is water as a gas and it is invisible. The white cloud is made of tiny water drops which are liquid.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for steam is a gas, 1 mark for invisible, 1 mark for white cloud being tiny drops, 1 mark for liquid, 1 mark for a clear explanation.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: They stay for many years, block drains, harm animals that eat them and pollute land and water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three points.

24. (5 marks)
   Answer: Form groups with roles. Wear gloves and shoes. Use rakes and shovels. Sort waste into decomposable and non-decomposable bins. Take compost to the pit. Wash hands after.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step up to 5.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: It keeps out dirt and leaves and stops mosquitoes from breeding in it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dirt, 1 mark for mosquitoes, 1 mark for making water safer.

26. (5 marks)
   Answer: Reduce wastage: close taps. Reuse: washing vegetables water on plants. Recycle: cleaning used water at a treatment plant or filtering. Include rainwater harvesting.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three methods, 1 mark for correct examples and 1 mark for harvesting.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: Push dry tissue into the bottom of the cup. Turn the cup upside down and push it straight down into water. Lift it out. The tissue is dry because air took up the space in the cup and kept the water out.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for set up, 1 mark for pushing into water, 1 mark for dry tissue, 1 mark for conclusion.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: They keep their shape so we can build houses, make tools, furniture, clothes and shoes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct use.
